#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/sig node
/priority important-longterm

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This promotes the EphemeralContainers feature to GA, updates documentation and removes feature gate checks.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #111030

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The graduation criteria from [KEP #277](https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-node/277-ephemeral-containers) are:

- [x] Ephemeral Containers have been in beta for at least 2 releases.
- [x] Ephemeral Containers see use in 3 projects or articles.
- [x] Ephemeral Container creation is covered by conformance tests.
  - Node conformance added in #111404
  - project-wide conformance follow-up in #111440
- [x] Fix: kubectl incorrectly suggests a debug container can be reattached after exit
  - Addressed in #111185 
- [x] Fix: `validateEphemeralContainers` adds a superfluous index to ephemeral container spec paths
  - Addressed in #111401

Notes: 

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
[Ephemeral Containers](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/ephemeral-containers/) are now generally available. The `EphemeralContainers` feature gate is always enabled and should be removed from `--feature-gates` flag on the kube-apiserver and the kubelet command lines. The `EphemeralContainers` feature gate is [deprecated and scheduled for removal](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecation) in a future release.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

Please use the following format for linking documentation:

issue_context.title: Promote Ephemeral Containers to GA
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue tracks the change required to update the `EphemeralContainers` feature gate to GA

### Why is this needed?

This promotes ephemeral containers to GA
comments:
According to https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/321b82a9d05acc5bd8b6aef5864b7a944c0d733c/keps/sig-node/277-ephemeral-containers/README.md#beta---ga-graduation

> ### Beta -> GA Graduation
> 
> - [x]  Ephemeral Containers have been in beta for at least 2 releases. （beta in v1.23）
> - [x]  Ephemeral Containers see use in 3 projects or articles.
> - [ ]  Ephemeral Container creation is covered by [conformance tests](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/conformance-tests.md). (Promote some test cases to conformance tests) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111025
> - [ ]  The following cosmetic codebase TODOs are resolved:
> - - [ ]  kubectl incorrectly suggests a debug container can be reattached after exit. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111027
> - - [ ]  validateEphemeralContainers adds a superfluous index to ephemeral container spec paths. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111028.

review_comments:
Do we want to keep this function now?

Is this a function that was added back then by ephemeralContainers or is it one of these abstractions that we always had "just in case" and we want to keep it?

We added the container visitor during ephemeral containers because it tipped complexity of visiting all containers over a threshold. We can retire `AllFeatureEnabledContainers()` if we don't think we're ever going to add another type of container.

If we do it, I recommend decoupling from this feature graduation and do it early in the next dev cycle so we don't cause a bunch of conflicts for people racing the the merge window.
I'd probably keep the method, just in case, but agree that either way, it shouldn't be changed in this PR

I'm not familiar with how GA migrations, sorry if the question is obvious. The strategy is to keep the feature here, enable it by default and just ignore it in the rest of the code (so it is effectively impossible to turn off)?

That's correct, the process is described here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/896f0cea19b3754f3f1cf4e803698bbc66fddbd6/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/feature-gates.md#ga-features

GA features are always enabled, but we give cluster operators a couple of releases to stop using the feature flags before we remove them.
idem for the comment in the other definition of `AllFeatureEnabledContainers()`
Why keep this as a comment vs deleting it? Curious, really
I remember having a lot of trouble tracking down this problem so I wanted to leave some documentation for the next person, but I don't feel strongly about it.
